comments.body: Example title with accented characters becomes stripped ASCII-ish garbage in Subject; HTML body is fine.

content.text: Example title with accented characters becomes stripped ASCII-ish garbage in Subject; HTML body is fine.

Notification emails whose issue titles include non-ASCII characters (e.g. accented names, CJK, emoji) arrive with those characters missing from the subject line. Body content retains the correct title.

Subject should preserve the same Unicode as the issue title. The mailer builds subjects with an ASCII-only header encoder path that strips bytes outside 0x20-0x7E instead of applying RFC 2047 encoded-words.
Recipients scanning inbox subjects cannot identify issues with localized titles. Switching subject encoding to UTF-8 encoded-word (or letting the ESP handle Unicode subjects) restores the full title.
